statement: With 10 minutes left, Ivo has five unanswered questions. He knows how long each would take him and that he would get each one right: three 5-point questions taking 4, 5 and 6 minutes, and two 3-point questions taking 2 and 3 minutes. What is the most points he can add in the 10 minutes?

choices.misconception: I did only the two 3-point questions, because they are the quickest.
I chose the two fastest 5-point questions, taking 4 and 5 minutes, and stopped with 1 minute left.
I picked the questions taking 2, 4 and 5 minutes without noticing that they need 11 minutes.
I counted all three 5-point questions without checking that they need 15 minutes.

hints: Which groups of questions fit into 10 minutes?
Triage means choosing by points for the time spent, not by points alone. List the groups of questions that fit within 10 minutes and compare their totals.
Two 5-pointers fit (4 + 5 = 9 minutes, 10 points). But the 2, 3 and 4 minute questions also take 9 minutes and give 3 + 3 + 5 points.

solutions.reliable: Three 5-point questions need 15 minutes, too long. Two 5-pointers and a 3-pointer need at least 4 + 5 + 2 = 11 minutes, also too long, so 13 points is impossible. The next best is one 5-pointer with both 3-pointers: 4 + 2 + 3 = 9 minutes for 5 + 3 + 3 = 11 points. Two 5-pointers alone give only 10. So the most is 11. The transferable idea: with limited time, compare points per minute and check which combinations fit, instead of grabbing the biggest questions first.

whyOnTest: Contest time is a budget: choosing which questions to do is itself a calculation, and the biggest questions are not always the best buy.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
